name: Levocardia

criteria.description: Heart apex located in the left hemithorax
Normal arrangement of abdominal and thoracic viscera (situs solitus)
No evidence of cardiac malposition such as dextrocardia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of heart apex in left hemithorax with situs solitus confirmed by imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Levocardia is a normal cardiac position but may be associated with congenital heart defects.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Heart apex located in left hemithorax
searchTerms: heart tip located on left side
heart positioned in left chest area

pathognomonic.symptomName: Normal situs solitus of thoracic and abdominal organs
searchTerms: normal organ arrangement in chest and abdomen

common.symptomName: Congenital heart defects (e.g., ventricular septal defect)
Respiratory distress due to associated cardiac anomalies
searchTerms: breathing problems due to heart defects
difficulty breathing caused by heart issues
low oxygen causing blue skin due to heart defects
failure to gain weight as baby

occasional.symptomName: Arrhythmias related to structural heart defects
searchTerms: arrhythmias linked to heart structure problems
abnormal heart rhythms due to heart abnormalities

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary hypertension secondary to cardiac defects
searchTerms: high blood pressure in lungs from heart defects
pulmonary hypertension caused by heart problems
lung blood vessel pressure increase due to heart issues

rare.symptomName: Hepatomegaly due to congestive heart failure
searchTerms: liver swelling due to congestive heart failure

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests unless secondary complications present
imaging: Chest X-ray showing heart apex on left side
Echocardiography confirming normal cardiac position and associated defects
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be associated with syndromic congenital heart diseases
other: Electrocardiogram may show abnormalities related to structural defects

distinguishingFeatures: Heart apex located in right hemithorax
Often associated with situs inversus or heterotaxy
Mirror-image reversal of thoracic and abdominal organs
Heart apex usually on right side

redFlags: Recurrent respiratory infections with failure to thrive
references: Anderson RH, et al. Levocardia and its clinical implications. Heart. 2018.
Moss AJ, et al. Congenital Heart Disease: Diagnosis and Management. 2020.
